correctness.rationale: Exact model, all p,q,t>0, mass-one simplex and independent unit-rate clocks specified. Two-event synchronous coupling has strict contraction 1/2+1/(4(1+p))+q/(4(1+q))<1 for all positive p,q, proving unique stationarity. Generator first and second moments close and yield the stated rational formulas; the global (p,q,t) covariance identity was independently cross-multiplied and verified as a sparse multivariate polynomial coefficient identity, with 103 additional exact tests of the p=4,q=2 covariance matrix. Finite sampling is not substituted for infinite parameter proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A known exact stationary mean is insufficient to determine covariances, as this family itself demonstrates by keeping means fixed while changing the covariance sign. Reversible Dirichlet conditioning would force strictly negative off-diagonals at fixed mass and is inconsistent with the model’s middle-site shape parameters; thus it does not imply the positive regime. The previously established positive association for the open harmonic model has a different generator, boundary sources and no fixed-total-mass constraint, so it neither predicts this sign reversal nor subsumes the formula. The new result is a natural finite-model refinement of a recognized moment gap, not a claim to have invented positivity of correlations.

value.rationale: The motivating paper identifies unknown joint mass moments as a mathematical gap. On the minimal nontrivial fixed-total chain, a complete two-parameter bias classification identifies exactly when tuning noise concentration alone reverses nearest-neighbor covariance while preserving the mean profile; it supplies a sharp non-Dirichlet fluctuation boundary and quantitative benchmarks. The theorem establishes an all-positive-parameter phase region, not merely an arbitrarily picked numeric slice or a re-expression of first-moment formulas.
